answer: Proof-of-work identity anchoring requires each new agent to burn computation by hashing a ferrous-tagged puzzle tied to its public key before it can transact. Like a river that only allows boats past a narrow ledge after checking their weight, the network verifies the proof cheaply but rejects missing work. An attacker spinning up thousands of Sybils must repeat the costly hashing for every fake identity, making mass deception more expensive than honest participation.
